events.text: {war_a} and {war_b} both send envoys to your door. Each wants your sword. Each promises the other side is the wicked one.

effects.log: You join the war. The murim takes note of whose side you chose.
You join the war. The murim takes note of whose side you chose.
Both envoys leave insulted. Neutrality has a price, but it is a fair one.

events.text: Refugees from the war between {war_a} and {war_b} fill the roads: villagers who had nothing to do with either sect.

effects.log: Your rice store empties. A hundred families eat through the winter.
A week on the road, two bandit gangs turned back, and a village of grateful strangers.

events.text: A wounded disciple of {war_a} collapses at your door, begging you to hide them from {war_b}.

effects.log: That night, {war_b} searches the street. They do not search your house. The disciple will never forget it.
You close the door. You hear the search party find them an hour later.

events.text: Both sides of the war between {war_a} and {war_b} are exhausted. Someone with enough fame could end it.

choices.text: Call them to a peace table

ok.log: Three days of shouting, one day of silence, and a treaty. The murim calls it your peace.

fail.log: The talks collapse on the first day. Both sides blame you a little.

effects.log: The war goes on without you.

events.text: A merchant offers you a fortune to escort weapons to whichever side of the war pays more.

effects.log: You grow rich on other people's war. The silver is heavy in more ways than one.
The merchant finds someone else. At least it was not you.

events.text: You cross a battlefield of the war between {war_a} and {war_b}. Broken swords, abandoned banners, and silence.

choices.text: Bury the dead of both sides

effects.log: It takes three days. Nobody thanks you, and that is fine.
A good sword, a pouch of silver, and a bad feeling.

events.text: Your sect is at war. The elders call every disciple to the front.

ok.log: You hold a mountain pass for a week. The sect will tell that story for a generation.

fail.deathCause: the war between two sects, at the front
fail.log: You hold, and pay for it in blood. The sect remembers you stood.

effects.log: Someone must protect the young disciples. It is not glorious, but it is not nothing.

events.text: In the middle of the war, you discover an elder of your own sect selling plans to the enemy.

effects.log: The elder is expelled. The war turns, a little, in your sect's favour.
The elder begs, and confesses everything. You let them leave quietly, with nothing.
